paper.title: Conformal Intent Classification and Clarification for Fast and Accurate Intent Recognition
paper.authors: Floris den Hengst, Ralf Wolter, Patrick Altmeyer, Arda Kaygan

source.licence: Repo: MIT. Underlying corpora: ACID (github.com/AmFamMLTeam/ACID@66bc5e0) has no licence file; ATIS is LDC-derived; BANKING77 CC-BY-4.0, CLINC150 CC-BY-3.0, HWU64 CC-BY-4.0, MTOD CC-BY-SA-4.0 (from the datasets' public cards; not verified further). Mixed/missing licences, so no utterance text is stored: the frozen files that scripts/prepare_cicc.py writes hold row coordinates, gold intent and a per-row SHA-256 of [text, gold]; the adapter rebuilds text from the clone and verifies every hash.
source.split_provenance: The released data/<dataset>/bert/{calibration,test}_predictions.csv are the exact calibration/test splits the paper evaluated (pretrain_<dataset>.ipynb: HF datasets train_test_split 60/20/20, stratified except ATIS, seed=1; the fine-tuned BERT softmax is stored per row). We use these files directly instead of re-running the split, so the split is identical by construction. Columns used: text, hash (0-based row id), label (index into labels.csv). The BERT scores are only used offline to validate the scoring port.
source.mtod_release: https://download.pytorch.org/data/multilingual_task_oriented_dialog_slotfilling.zip (fb.me/multilingual_task_oriented_data), sha256 fdd3ab27570f0d9c3a692260c69c53c5bc5dfff145dadfc428d72b93566b5fce; used only to recover the domain of each MTOD intent (en/*.tsv column 1, 12 domain/intent labels, 43,323 rows = paper Table 1) for the prompt criteria.

excluded: The Dutch industry dataset IND (not released, and not English) and the B77/DFCX setting (commercial Dialogflow CX scores, not a replaceable open predictor). Free-form clarification-question wording (Vicuna) is not scored.

atis.note: random (non-stratified) split, as in the paper

c150.note: C150-IS: the release's test file has 3,845 rows incl. 240 `oos`; they are dropped as in cicc_clinc150_bert.ipynb (df_test = test[label != 42]). Jev's inventory excludes `oos` (the paper's BERT was trained without OOS rows; its oos output is untrained).

hwu64.note: the release has 68 intent labels although the paper calls the set HWU64

c150_oos.construction: cicc_clinc150_bert.ipynb cell 3 replayed on row ids: np.random.seed(42); OOS pool (ood_predictions.csv, 1,200) shuffled; 1,200 in-scope test rows sampled (unused draw, kept for RNG state); OOS-calibration = 1,200 calibration rows + 600 OOS; OOS-test = 1,200 in-scope test rows + 600 OOS. Verified against the notebook's printed X_ood_test (first/last five ids, 1,800 rows).

b77_oos.construction: cicc_banking77_bert.ipynb cell 3: np.random.seed(42); ATIS pool (banking77/bert/atis_predictions.csv, 5,871 ATIS utterances labelled 77=oos) shuffled; B77 test shuffled; OOS-calibration = second half of the test (1,309) + ATIS[1308:] (4,563); OOS-test = first half of the test (1,308) + ATIS[:1308] (1,308). The conformal quantile always uses the B77 calibration split.

english_verification.method: All 58,589 frozen utterance rows (calibration + test of the six datasets, C150 OOS pool, B77's ATIS pool) screened with langid 1.1.6 (normalised; flag non-en with p > 0.99 and >= 4 tokens) and a non-ASCII character check; flags in data/frozen/cicc/language_screen.json.
english_verification.result: All 152 flags inspected: every one is English (langid confusions on short MTOD commands such as 'Temperature tonight near Karachi Fahrenheit' -> de, 'do i need an umbrella today' -> it; non-ASCII only currency symbols £/€, curly apostrophes and an ellipsis). No rows dropped; N equals the release.
english_verification.datasets: All six are English-language benchmarks by construction (paper Section 4: 'six public intent recognition data sets in English'); MTOD uses only its English part (the authors' convert_mtod.py also writes es/th, which the paper does not use).

prompt.files: prompts/cicc_{acid,atis,b77,c150,hwu64,mtod}.json (written by scripts/prepare_cicc.py; OOS tasks reuse the in-scope prompt so their requests hit the same cache entries)
prompt.primitive: choice over the full intent inventory (max 175 options, ACID; below the 255-option limit, no decomposition)
prompt.criteria: released intent names rendered with the authors' label.replace('_', ' ') (their notebooks and Appendix B tables); MTOD adds the release domain (e.g. weather/find). No intent definitions exist in any release.
prompt.instruction: one sentence naming the assistant context from each dataset paper + 'choose the single intent'.
prompt.truncation: utterance cut at 36,000 chars; longest frozen request is 9,055 chars (ACID, incl. criteria); n_truncated = 0 for every task

validation_offline.bert_replay: The scoring port (MAPIE 0.6.5 'score' quantile and set rule; src/eval.py cq_stats; heuristics B1-B3; notebook OOS procedure) run on the released BERT probabilities reproduces the release's results/results.csv to all printed digits for ACID, ATIS, C150, HWU64, MTOD (CICC and B1-B3) and B77 at alpha=.02; Table 3 C150-OOS CICC F1 .0676 / AUROC .878 and CICC-OOS 1-alpha .99558, th 6, F1 .9054 / AUROC .970 (notebook cells 23-26, 41 exactly); B77-OOS CICC (alpha .02) F1 .757 / AUROC .915 and CICC-OOS 1-alpha .9938, th 6, F1 .903 / AUROC .967 (paper .76/.92 and .994/6/.90/.97).
validation_offline.synthetic: gold one-hot answers give coverage 1, Single 1, accuracy 1 on every in-scope task; all 68,388 requests (55,425 unique bodies) build and serialise.

deviations: B77 alpha: Tables 2/3 print 1-alpha = .97 but the reported numbers were produced at alpha = .02 (authors' index_for_arange(.01,.01,.03) truncates to index 1). We run at .98 and also report .97.
B77-OOS alpha grid start 1/5871 is a reconstruction (the notebook references an undefined y_ood); C150 uses the notebook's 1/2400. Grid values below 1/(n_cal+1) are skipped (MAPIE rejects them).
Paper Table 2 B77/BERT Single .73 and |CQ| 2.84 are not reproducible from the released outputs at any alpha (.02 gives .79 / 2.90, matching results.csv and Tables 8/9).
Jev inventory for C150 has 150 intents (no `oos` option), matching the in-scope BERT training.
